antibody.assumptions: MW=149 kDa, hl_csf=8h, hl_tissue=24h, Kup=0.01/min (MW-scaled), dose=5mg
antibody.parameter_sensitivity: Higher MW → lower tissue uptake → larger relative improvement (more drug lost without architecture)

oligonucleotide.assumptions: MW=7 kDa, hl_csf=12h, hl_tissue=72h, Kup=0.005/min, dose=40mg
oligonucleotide.parameter_sensitivity: Lower MW → higher tissue uptake → smaller relative improvement (less drug lost to drain)

gene_therapy.assumptions: MW=5000 kDa, hl_csf=24h, hl_tissue=168h, Kup=0.002/min, dose=0.1mg
gene_therapy.parameter_sensitivity: Very high MW → very low tissue uptake → very large relative improvement (most drug lost without architecture)

small_molecule.assumptions: MW=0.45 kDa, hl_csf=4h, hl_tissue=8h, Kup=0.03/min, dose=12mg
small_molecule.parameter_sensitivity: Very low MW → very high tissue uptake → smallest relative improvement (drug reaches tissue quickly regardless)

note: All results are MODEL_DERIVED. The advantage is largest for high-MW agents (more drug lost to drainage without architecture) and smallest for small molecules (rapid tissue uptake). This is consistent with the mechanism: the architecture reduces drainage-mediated loss, which matters more for agents that are slowly taken up by tissue.
